page: Microsoft Azure D192ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 192 vCPUs mapped to 96 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 11,339 GB of local storage. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 10% of tested systems. The server demonstrates high memory bandwidth, reaching 13,906.45 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 677.36 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. However, single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and PassMark memory scores falling into the middle 50%. Large-scale parallel tasks, such as multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Redis SET operations, perform in the top 10%, while LLM text generation speeds vary from weak for small models to average for large models.

Given its high resource density, the D192ds_v7 offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring massive parallel processing and high-capacity local storage without the overhead of dedicated GPU hardware. The combination of 192 vCPUs, 768.0 GB of RAM, and 11,339 GB of local storage makes this instance highly suitable for large-scale database operations, high-throughput static web serving, heavy multi-threaded data compression, and CPU-bound machine learning inference tasks.
